NKJV.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
NKJV.2: “Therefore my anxious thoughts make me answer, Because of the turmoil within me.
NKJV.3: I have heard the rebuke that reproaches me, And the spirit of my understanding causes me to answer.
NKJV.4: “Do you not know this of old, Since man was placed on earth,
NKJV.5: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, And the joy of the hypocrite is but for a moment?
NKJV.6: Though his haughtiness mounts up to the heavens, And his head reaches to the clouds,
NKJV.7: Yet he will perish forever like his own refuse; Those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’
NKJV.8: He will fly away like a dream, and not be found; Yes, he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
NKJV.9: The eye that saw him will see him no more, Nor will his place behold him anymore.
NKJV.10: His children will seek the favor of the poor, And his hands will restore his wealth.
NKJV.11: His bones are full of his youthful vigor,  But it will lie down with him in the dust.
NKJV.12: “Though evil is sweet in his mouth, And he hides it under his tongue,
NKJV.13: Though he spares it and does not forsake it, But still keeps it in his mouth,
NKJV.14: Yet his food in his stomach turns sour; It becomes cobra venom within him.
NKJV.15: He swallows down riches And vomits them up again; God casts them out of his belly.
NKJV.16: He will suck the poison of cobras; The viper’s tongue will slay him.
NKJV.17: He will not see the streams, The rivers flowing with honey and cream.
NKJV.18: He will restore that for which he labored, And will not swallow it down; From the proceeds of business He will get no enjoyment.
NKJV.19: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor, He has violently seized a house which he did not build.
NKJV.20: “Because  he knows no quietness in his heart, He will not save anything he desires.
NKJV.21: Nothing is left for him to eat; Therefore his well-being will not last.
NKJV.22: In his self-sufficiency he will be in distress; Every hand of misery will come against him.
NKJV.23: When he is about to fill his stomach, God will cast on him the fury of His wrath, And will rain it on him while he is eating.
NKJV.24: He will flee from the iron weapon; A bronze bow will pierce him through.
NKJV.25: It is drawn, and comes out of the body; Yes, the glittering point comes out of his gall. Terrors come upon him;
NKJV.26: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. An unfanned fire will consume him; It shall go ill with him who is left in his tent.
NKJV.27: The heavens will reveal his iniquity, And the earth will rise up against him.
NKJV.28: The increase of his house will depart, And his goods will flow away in the day of His wrath.
NKJV.29: This is the portion from God for a wicked man, The heritage appointed to him by God.”

ESV.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
ESV.2: “Therefore my thoughts answer me, because of my haste within me.
ESV.3: I hear censure that insults me, and out of my understanding a spirit answers me.
ESV.4: Do you not know this from of old, since man was placed on earth,
ESV.5: that the exulting of the wicked is short, and the joy of the godless but for a moment?
ESV.6: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,
ESV.7: he will perish forever like his own dung; those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’
ESV.8: He will fly away like a dream and not be found; he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
ESV.9: The eye that saw him will see him no more, nor will his place any more behold him.
ESV.10: His children will seek the favor of the poor, and his hands will give back his wealth.
ESV.11: His bones are full of his youthful vigor, but it will lie down with him in the dust.
ESV.12: “Though evil is sweet in his mouth, though he hides it under his tongue,
ESV.13: though he is loath to let it go and holds it in his mouth,
ESV.14: yet his food is turned in his stomach; it is the venom of cobras within him.
ESV.15: He swallows down riches and vomits them up again; God casts them out of his belly.
ESV.16: He will suck the poison of cobras; the tongue of a viper will kill him.
ESV.17: He will not look upon the rivers, the streams flowing with honey and curds.
ESV.18: He will give back the fruit of his toil and will not swallow it down; from the profit of his trading he will get no enjoyment.
ESV.19: For he has crushed and abandoned the poor; he has seized a house that he did not build.
ESV.20: “Because he knew no contentment in his belly, he will not let anything in which he delights escape him.
ESV.21: There was nothing left after he had eaten; therefore his prosperity will not endure.
ESV.22: In the fullness of his sufficiency he will be in distress; the hand of everyone in misery will come against him.
ESV.23: To fill his belly to the full, God  will send his burning anger against him and rain it upon him into his body.
ESV.24: He will flee from an iron weapon; a bronze arrow will strike him through.
ESV.25: It is drawn forth and comes out of his body; the glittering point comes out of his gallbladder; terrors come upon him.
ESV.26: Utter darkness is laid up for his treasures; a fire not fanned will devour him; what is left in his tent will be consumed.
ESV.27: The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
ESV.28: The possessions of his house will be carried away, dragged off in the day of God's  wrath.
ESV.29: This is the wicked man's portion from God, the heritage decreed for him by God.”

WEB.2: “Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
WEB.3: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.
WEB.4: Don’t you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,
WEB.5: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?
WEB.6: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,
WEB.7: yet he shall perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him shall say, ‘Where is he?’
WEB.8: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found. Yes, he shall be chased away like a vision of the night.
WEB.9: The eye which saw him shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more see him.
WEB.10: His children shall seek the favor of the poor. His hands shall give back his wealth.
WEB.11: His bones are full of his youth, but youth shall lie down with him in the dust.
WEB.12: “Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,
WEB.13: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth;
WEB.14: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.
WEB.15: He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.
WEB.16: He shall suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue shall kill him.
WEB.17: He shall not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.
WEB.18: That for which he labored he shall restore, and shall not swallow it down. According to the substance that he has gotten, he shall not rejoice.
WEB.19: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he shall not build it up.
WEB.20: “Because he knew no quietness within him, he shall not save anything of that in which he delights.
WEB.21: There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
WEB.22: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress shall overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery shall come on him.
WEB.23: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.
WEB.24: He shall flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow shall strike him through.
WEB.25: He draws it out, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.
WEB.26: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire shall devour him. It shall consume that which is left in his tent.
WEB.27: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity. The earth shall rise up against him.
WEB.28: The increase of his house shall depart. They shall rush away in the day of his wrath.
WEB.29: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God.”

NLT.2:
“I must reply
because I am greatly disturbed.
NLT.3:
I’ve had to endure your insults,
but now my spirit prompts me to reply.
NLT.4:
“Don’t you realize that from the beginning of time,
ever since people were first placed on the earth,
NLT.5:
the triumph of the wicked has been short lived
and the joy of the godless has been only temporary?
NLT.6:
Though the pride of the godless reaches to the heavens
and their heads touch the clouds,
NLT.7:
yet they will vanish forever,
thrown away like their own dung.
Those who knew them will ask,
‘Where are they?’
NLT.8:
They will fade like a dream and not be found.
They will vanish like a vision in the night.
NLT.9:
Those who once saw them will see them no more.
Their families will never see them again.
NLT.10:
Their children will beg from the poor,
for they must give back their stolen riches.
NLT.11:
Though they are young,
their bones will lie in the dust.
NLT.12:
“They enjoyed the sweet taste of wickedness,
letting it melt under their tongue.
NLT.13:
They savored it,
holding it long in their mouths.
NLT.14:
But suddenly the food in their bellies turns sour,
a poisonous venom in their stomach.
NLT.15:
They will vomit the wealth they swallowed.
God won’t let them keep it down.
NLT.16:
They will suck the poison of cobras.
The viper will kill them.
NLT.17:
They will never again enjoy streams of olive oil
or rivers of milk and honey.
NLT.18:
They will give back everything they worked for.
Their wealth will bring them no joy.
NLT.19:
For they oppressed the poor and left them destitute.
They foreclosed on their homes.
NLT.20:
They were always greedy and never satisfied.
Nothing remains of all the things they dreamed about.
NLT.21:
Nothing is left after they finish gorging themselves.
Therefore, their prosperity will not endure.
NLT.22:
“In the midst of plenty, they will run into trouble
and be overcome by misery.
NLT.23:
May God give them a bellyful of trouble.
May God rain down his anger upon them.
NLT.24:
When they try to escape an iron weapon,
a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce them.
NLT.25:
The arrow is pulled from their back,
and the arrowhead glistens with blood.
The terrors of death are upon them.
NLT.26:
Their treasures will be thrown into deepest darkness.
A wildfire will devour their goods,
consuming all they have left.
NLT.27:
The heavens will reveal their guilt,
and the earth will testify against them.
NLT.28:
A flood will sweep away their house.
God’s anger will descend on them in torrents.
NLT.29:
This is the reward that God gives the wicked.
It is the inheritance decreed by God.”

AMP.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,
AMP.2:
"Therefore my disquieting thoughts make me answer,
Because of the uneasiness that is within me.
AMP.3:
"I have heard the reproof which insults me,
But the spirit of my understanding makes me answer.
AMP.4:
"Do you not know this from the old days,
Since the time that man was placed on the earth,
AMP.5:
That the triumphing of the wicked is short,
And the joy of the godless is only for a moment?
AMP.6:
"Though his pride reaches the heavens
And his head touches the clouds,
AMP.7:
Yet he perishes forever like his own refuse;
Those who have seen him will say, 'Where is he?'
AMP.8:
"He flies away like a dream and cannot be found;
Yes, he is chased away like a vision of the night.
AMP.9:
"The eye which saw him sees him no longer,
Neither does his [accustomed] place behold him any longer.
AMP.10:
"His sons favor the poor [and pay his obligations],
And his hands give back his [ill-gotten] wealth.
AMP.11:
"His bones are full of youthful strength
But it lies down with him in the dust.
AMP.12:
"Though evil and wickedness are sweet in his mouth
And he hides it under his tongue,
AMP.13:
Though he desires it and will not let it go
But holds it in his mouth,
AMP.14:
Yet his food turns [to poison] in his stomach;
It is the venom of vipers within him.
AMP.15:
"He swallows [his ill-gotten] riches,
But will vomit them up;
God will drive them out of his belly.
AMP.16:
"He sucks the poison of vipers [which ill-gotten wealth contains];
The viper's tongue slays him.
AMP.17:
"He does not look at the rivers,
The flowing streams of honey and butter [to enjoy his wealth].
AMP.18:
"He gives back what he has labored for and attained
And cannot swallow it [down to enjoy it];
As to the riches of his labor,
He cannot even enjoy them.
AMP.19:
"For he has oppressed and neglected the poor;
He has violently taken away houses which he did not build.
AMP.20:
"Because he knew no quietness or calm within him [because of his greed],
He does not retain anything he desires.
AMP.21:
"There is nothing left of what he devoured;
Therefore his prosperity does not endure.
AMP.22:
"In the fullness of his excess (great abundance) he will be in trouble;
The hand of everyone who suffers will come against him [he is miserable on every side].
AMP.23:
"When he fills his belly,
God will send His fierce anger on him
And will rain it upon him while he is eating.
AMP.24:
"He may flee from the iron weapon,
But the bow of bronze will pierce him through.
AMP.25:
"The arrow is drawn forth and it comes out of his back [after passing through his body];
Yes, the glittering point comes out of his gall.
Terrors march in upon him;
AMP.26:
Complete darkness (misfortune) is held in reserve for his treasures.
An unfanned fire will devour him;
It will consume the survivor in his tent.
AMP.27:
"The heavens will reveal his wickedness and guilt,
And the earth will rise up against him.
AMP.28:
"The produce and increase of his house will depart [with the victors];
His possessions will be dragged away in the day of God's wrath.
AMP.29:
"This is the wicked man's portion from God,
And the heritage decreed and appointed to him by God."

MSG.1: Zophar from Naamath again took his turn:
MSG.2:
"I can't believe what I'm hearing!
You've put my teeth on edge, my stomach in a knot.
MSG.3:
How dare you insult my intelligence like this!
Well, here's a piece of my mind!
MSG.4:
"Don't you even know the basics,
how things have been since the earliest days,
when Adam and Eve were first placed on earth?
MSG.5:
The good times of the wicked are short-lived;
godless joy is only momentary.
MSG.6:
The evil might become world famous,
strutting at the head of the celebrity parade,
MSG.7:
But still end up in a pile of dung.
Acquaintances look at them with disgust and say, 'What's that?'
MSG.8:
They fly off like a dream that can't be remembered,
like a shadowy illusion that vanishes in the light.
MSG.9:
Though once notorious public figures, now they're nobodies,
unnoticed, whether they come or go.
MSG.10:
Their children will go begging on skid row,
and they'll have to give back their ill-gotten gain.
MSG.11:
Right in the prime of life,
and youthful and vigorous, they'll die.
MSG.12:
"They savor evil as a delicacy,
roll it around on their tongues,
MSG.13:
Prolong the flavor, a dalliance in decadence—
real gourmets of evil!
MSG.14:
But then they get stomach cramps,
a bad case of food poisoning.
MSG.15:
They gag on all that rich food;
God makes them vomit it up.
MSG.16:
They gorge on evil, make a diet of that poison—
a deadly diet—and it kills them.
MSG.17:
No quiet picnics for them beside gentle streams
with fresh-baked bread and cheese, and tall, cool drinks.
MSG.18:
They spit out their food half-chewed,
unable to relax and enjoy anything they've worked for.
MSG.19:
And why? Because they exploited the poor,
took what never belonged to them.
MSG.20:
"Such God-denying people are never content with what they have
or who they are;
their greed drives them relentlessly.
MSG.21:
They plunder everything
but they can't hold on to any of it.
MSG.22:
Just when they think they have it all, disaster strikes;
they're served up a plate full of misery.
MSG.23:
When they've filled their bellies with that,
God gives them a taste of his anger,
and they get to chew on that for a while.
MSG.24:
As they run for their lives from one disaster,
they run smack into another.
MSG.25:
They're knocked around from pillar to post,
beaten to within an inch of their lives.
They're trapped in a house of horrors,
MSG.26:
and see their loot disappear down a black hole.
Their lives are a total loss—
not a penny to their name, not so much as a bean.
MSG.27:
God will strip them of their sin-soaked clothes
and hang their dirty laundry out for all to see.
MSG.28:
Life is a complete wipeout for them,
nothing surviving God's wrath.
MSG.29:
There! That's God's blueprint for the wicked—
what they have to look forward to."

NRSVCE.2:
“Pay attention! My thoughts urge me to answer,
because of the agitation within me.
NRSVCE.3:
I hear censure that insults me,
and a spirit beyond my understanding answers me.
NRSVCE.4:
Do you not know this from of old,
ever since mortals were placed on earth,
NRSVCE.5:
that the exulting of the wicked is short,
and the joy of the godless is but for a moment?
NRSVCE.6:
Even though they mount up high as the heavens,
and their head reaches to the clouds,
NRSVCE.7:
they will perish forever like their own dung;
those who have seen them will say, ‘Where are they?’
NRSVCE.8:
They will fly away like a dream, and not be found;
they will be chased away like a vision of the night.
NRSVCE.9:
The eye that saw them will see them no more,
nor will their place behold them any longer.
NRSVCE.10:
Their children will seek the favor of the poor,
and their hands will give back their wealth.
NRSVCE.11:
Their bodies, once full of youth,
will lie down in the dust with them.
NRSVCE.12:
“Though wickedness is sweet in their mouth,
though they hide it under their tongues,
NRSVCE.13:
though they are loath to let it go,
and hold it in their mouths,
NRSVCE.14:
yet their food is turned in their stomachs;
it is the venom of asps within them.
NRSVCE.15:
They swallow down riches and vomit them up again;
God casts them out of their bellies.
NRSVCE.16:
They will suck the poison of asps;
the tongue of a viper will kill them.
NRSVCE.17:
They will not look on the rivers,
the streams flowing with honey and curds.
NRSVCE.18:
They will give back the fruit of their toil,
and will not swallow it down;
from the profit of their trading
they will get no enjoyment.
NRSVCE.19:
For they have crushed and abandoned the poor,
they have seized a house that they did not build.
NRSVCE.20:
“They knew no quiet in their bellies;
in their greed they let nothing escape.
NRSVCE.21:
There was nothing left after they had eaten;
therefore their prosperity will not endure.
NRSVCE.22:
In full sufficiency they will be in distress;
all the force of misery will come upon them.
NRSVCE.23:
To fill their belly to the full
God will send his fierce anger into them,
and rain it upon them as their food.
NRSVCE.24:
They will flee from an iron weapon;
a bronze arrow will strike them through.
NRSVCE.25:
It is drawn forth and comes out of their body,
and the glittering point comes out of their gall;
terrors come upon them.
NRSVCE.26:
Utter darkness is laid up for their treasures;
a fire fanned by no one will devour them;
what is left in their tent will be consumed.
NRSVCE.27:
The heavens will reveal their iniquity,
and the earth will rise up against them.
NRSVCE.28:
The possessions of their house will be carried away,
dragged off in the day of God’s wrath.
NRSVCE.29:
This is the portion of the wicked from God,
the heritage decreed for them by God.”

NET.2: “This is why my troubled thoughts bring me back — because of my feelings within me.
NET.3: When I hear a reproof that dishonors me, then my understanding prompts me to answer.
NET.4: “Surely you know that it has been from old, ever since humankind was placed on the earth,
NET.5: that the elation of the wicked is brief, the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.
NET.6: Even though his stature reaches to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,
NET.7: he will perish forever, like his own excrement; those who used to see him will say, ‘Where is he?’
NET.8: Like a dream he flies away, never again to be found, and like a vision of the night he is put to flight.
NET.9: People who had seen him will not see him again, and the place where he was will recognize him no longer.
NET.10: His sons must recompense the poor; his own hands must return his wealth.
NET.11: His bones were full of his youthful vigor, but that vigor will lie down with him in the dust.
NET.12: “If evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
NET.13: if he retains it for himself and does not let it go, and holds it fast in his mouth,
NET.14: his food is turned sour in his stomach; it becomes the venom of serpents within him.
NET.15: The wealth that he consumed he vomits up, God will make him throw it out of his stomach.
NET.16: He sucks the poison of serpents; the fangs of a viper kill him.
NET.17: He will not look on the streams, the rivers, which are the torrents of honey and butter.
NET.18: He gives back the ill-gotten gain without assimilating it; he will not enjoy the wealth from his commerce.
NET.19: For he has oppressed the poor and abandoned them; he has seized a house which he did not build.
NET.20: For he knows no satisfaction in his appetite; he does not let anything he desires escape.
NET.21: “Nothing is left for him to devour; that is why his prosperity does not last.
NET.22: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress overtakes him. the full force of misery will come upon him.
NET.23: “While he is filling his belly, God sends his burning anger against him, and rains down his blows upon him.
NET.24: If he flees from an iron weapon, then an arrow from a bronze bow pierces him.
NET.25: When he pulls it out and it comes out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver, terrors come over him.
NET.26: Total darkness waits to receive his treasures; a fire which has not been kindled will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
NET.27: The heavens reveal his iniquity; the earth rises up against him.
NET.28: A flood will carry off his house, rushing waters on the day of God’s wrath.
NET.29: Such is the lot God allots the wicked, and the heritage of his appointment from God.”
